item.title: Table tennis: BVB back to winning ways
item.description: Table tennis: BVB back to winning ways Team news Fadeev skilfully used his players’ disappointment at the sobering result in Bremen as motivation for the clash with the 2025 double winners. With star player Anders Lind and former doubles world champion Kristian Karlsson both sidelined through injury, the 51-year-old once again put his faith in summer signings Wim Verdonschot at number one and Joao Geraldo at number three. The coach made just one change, at number two: Adam Szudi replaced Cedric Nuytinck. The Hungarian, one of last season’s surprise performers, thus made his first appearance of the season. How the match unfolded The 600 spectators witnessed a match full of twists and turns in all three singles contests, making for a particularly thrilling encounter. In the opening singles, young international Verdonschot needed a deciding game to beat Tiago Abiodun despite twice taking the lead, as did Szudi against Ochsenhausen’s doubles world champion Shunsuke Togami in the next match. Geraldo also saw Iulian Chirita draw level at 1-1 before securing a four-game victory. Adam Szudi was undoubtedly the celebrated “Man of the Match” as BVB claimed their third consecutive win over Ochsenhausen. The 30-year-old repeatedly caught Togami, ranked 15th in the world, off guard. Szudi, primarily a doubles specialist who made his mark last season with eight wins in 18 singles matches, coped surprisingly well with his Japanese opponent’s powerful play and frequently took the initiative himself. All too often, Togami had no answer. Szudi was understandably delighted after his upset win: “You don’t beat a reigning world champion every day.” The right-hander’s surprise victory played a key role in Dortmund’s third-most emphatic Bundesliga win. BVB have conceded fewer than five games in a 3-0 victory on only two occasions: in November 2024 during their debut season against TTC OE Bad Homburg (four games), and just over three months ago this season against ASC Grünwettersbach (one game). Reaction Ursula Reitemeyer (Head of Table Tennis): “Our boys gave 110 per cent. Adam’s win against Togami was sensational. With our fans acting as our ‘twelfth man’, the team more than made up for the defeat against Bremen. We’ll keep pushing.” Evgeny Fadeev (Coach): “What a response after the 3-0 defeat in Bremen! A superb performance from everyone, a real team victory. Afterwards in the dressing room, we were asking ourselves how we could look like a completely different team just 48 hours after Bremen. But our in-depth discussions about the Bremen match and the lessons we learned from that defeat clearly paid off. That gave me a really good feeling going into this match, and absolutely everyone stayed focused right to the end. Adam’s win against Togami provided the decisive turning point, because it really was a breakthrough, a point against a world champion that none of us could have expected – and in his first match of the season. item.title: Bears Must Lock Up Theo Benedet And Jonah Jackson Now
item.description: Mike Dinovo-Imagn Images Since Caleb Williams remains on a cheap rookie deal, the front office has room to spend big on the players who actually make the team win. The logic behind each move is sound as Sports Illustrated reports that four Bears secured contract extensions for 2027 and beyond. The team has proven it can find value, and now it must pay for it before the market does. The most urgent case involves Theo Benedet. After losing the starting left tackle competition at camp, he assumed the position when Braxton Jones suffered a season-ending injury. He did not panic. Benedet has allowed only one sack and 18 pressures while maintaining a pass-blocking grade of 68.4 through nine games, according to reports. In the run game, he ranks 19th among tackles in the NFL with a 73.3 grade. Waiting is a poor strategy even though the Bears hold complete authority over him once he becomes an exclusive rights free agent following this season. A player who holds the line this well deserves a long-term deal as a potential swing tackle or starter. Jackson’s Turnaround Demands Cash Then there is Jonah Jackson, a story of redemption that the Bears must finish. After the team acquired him in a 2025 trade with the Rams, his career appeared finished because he missed most of that season due to injury. This season has been particularly impressive, with Jackson ranking fourth in run-blocking grade at 85.1 and fifth in overall grade at 83.1 among guards while not permitting a sack. Although he is under contract for another year, he has no guaranteed money left on his deal. That makes him a perfect candidate for a long-term extension. Locking him up now also lowers his $12.2 million cap hit for 2027. Future Plans for D’Marco Jackson The report also highlights linebacker D’Marco Jackson, who started his ascension last season as a pleasant surprise for Chicago. He is another player whose play has earned him a spot on the extension list. The team has the flexibility to keep these core pieces together while Caleb Williams matures. The Bears are 7-2 and sitting in first place in the NFC North, so keeping the offensive line solid is the smartest play they can make. Sports Illustrated reports that the team may allocate resources to players who have demonstrated their value while in Chicago. With a strong 7-2 record marking the midway point of the 2026 season, the Bears have landed their bye in an ideal spot to take stock of these performances.

item.title: Michigan football vs Oregon game day injuries: OT Blake Frazier is out
item.description: Michigan football will have a new offensive line configuration on the West Coast. U-M (5-4, 2-4 Big Ten) will be without offensive tackle Blake Frazier in the Week 11 contest against Oregon (6-3, 4-2 Big Ten). He left last week's loss to MSU in the second half and was officially ruled out in the pregame availability report provided to the Big Ten two hours before kickoff (3:30 p.m., FS1). The Wolverines could also be without right guard Brady Norton, who got banged up a week ago as well and played just 26 snaps. Norton, who's listed as a game-time decision, missed Michigan's Week 7 win over Penn State but has been a consistent part of the rotation, playing 446 snaps (the fourth most of any offensive lineman on the team) this year. Elsewhere, Michigan is down a rotational wide receiver in Channing Goodwin. The junior wideout only has two grabs for 32 yards this season but is frequently on the field, having played the third-most snaps (127) of any wideout, though Salesi Moa and Travis Johnson has been earning more playing time of late. Tight ends Hogan Hansen and Jalen Hoffman, who were listed as questionable all week, were both removed from the report. Hansen missed the first two games of the season and then was banged up last week, playing just six snaps. Hoffman hasn't missed any time yet this season. MICHIGAN VS OREGON PREDICTION: Will OC change make a difference? U-M got good news on the defensive side of the ball. Edge rushers John Henry Daley and Dom Nichols and safety Rod Moore were all listed as questionable but have been removed from the report, indicating all are good to go. The only player missing (who hasn't been out the whole year) on the defensive side of the ball is edge Nate Marshall, who was suspended indefinitely earlier this week. Tony Garcia is the Michigan beat writer for the Detroit Free Press. Email him at apgarcia@freepress.com and follow him on X at @RealTonyGarcia . item.description: Texas Longhorns setter Ella Swindle (1) celebrates a score during the NCAA Regional Final volleyball match against Wisconsin at Gregory Gym on Sunday, Dec. 14, 2025 in Austin. After an emotional postgame senior night celebration that included rounds of hugs and even more tears, Swindle confirmed to reporters after the match that she plans to leave Texas (14-8, 10-4 SEC) following this year, which continues Sunday against LSU in the regular-season finale. The Texas Longhorns celebrate beating Texas A&M in the Lone Star Showdown volleyball match at Gregory Gym on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. But I'm just praying about it a lot, and I know there's a really great plan in store. I've just been where my feet are and focusing on the moment that I'm in, but I'm definitely getting excited for what's next." Swindle's departure comes as no surprise, especially after fellow 2023 recruiting class members Torrey Stafford , Nya Bunton and Ramsey Gary announced their decision earlier this week to return to Texas for the 2027 season. Swindle and defensive specialist Anja Kujundžić were not a part of that announcement even though both four-year players still have one remaining year of eligibility. Both partook in Friday's senior night celebration. Setter in and out of rotation since freshman season By now, most Longhorn fans understand Swindle's saga. She served as the second setter to Averi Carlson as a sophomore before regaining the starting job last season. item.description: Douglas Lambert, Rory Underwood, Josh Lewsey and Henry Arundell are the other players to have scored five tries in a single match for England [Getty Images] Nations Championship England (49) 78 Tries: Joseph 5, Steward, Genge, Murley, Earl, Martin, B Curry, M Smith, Fisilau Cons: Ford 4, Slade Pen: Ford Japan (10) 15 Tries: Dearns, Helu Con: Saito Pen: Saito Will Joseph marked his comeback after four years out the Test game with a record-equalling five tries as England tore through Japan and set their sights on New Zealand next weekend. A teenage Joseph made his debut as a late replacement in a game against Australia four years ago. Since then he has endured his boyhood club London Irish going bust, an underwhelming spell at Harlequins and the loss of hearing in his left ear after an auto-immune reaction. But his superb early season form for Gloucester has thrust him back into the international picture and he took his opportunity superbly, showing work-rate and intelligence as well as raw top-end speed. Four other players - Douglas Lambert, Rory Underwood, Josh Lewsey and Henry Arundell - have scored five tries in a single match for England. Japan were vastly over-matched, unable to rev up the ball movement and quickfire rucks that have made them a threat to the game's major powers in the past. With the outcome clear as England raced out to a 32-3 lead inside 20 minutes, the focus sharpened on a number of individuals attempting to press their case alongside Joseph. Centre Max Ojomoh, making his first appearance since an excellent performance against Argentina 12 months ago, was smart and sharp in midfield. The Bath man burst into a pocket of space to help set up Joseph's second and his slick hands opened up a corridor of space for his team-mate's gleefully acrobatic fourth as Japan were buried beneath an avalanche of points. Henry Pollock, afforded only his second start in his eye-catching England career, carried gamely but didn't have the impact he has shown so often off the bench. Replacement Greg Fisilau's pair of wince-inducing hits and burrowing try added more intrigue to the back-row equation. And while George Ford sewed together England's backline neatly enough, his failure to convert more of England's early tries won't help his hopes of regaining the 10 shirt on a more permanent basis. item.title: 🔥 In-demand Antonio Nusa continues post-World Cup form for Norway
item.description: 🔥 In-demand Antonio Nusa continues post-World Cup form for Norway Norway's resurgence on the European stage at both the club and international level has been something brilliant for Nordic football. Though Erling Haaland will undoubtedly continue to receive the attention he so richly deserves, and much of the same can be said of captain Martin Ødegaard, the supporting cast for Ståle Solbakken's Røde, Hvite, Blå deserves plenty of praise. Antonio Nusa, perhaps, more than any other. Still just 21, the RB Leipzig starlet has been in some of the finest form of his career after a very credible summer with Norway at the 2026 World Cup. That hot streak continued this evening in Oslo when he opened the scoring in Norway's Nations League A home clash against Wales, meaning Nusa has now found the back of the net or collected an assist in six-straight matches for club and country since his brace of helpers against Elversberg back on 24 October. Taking up his position on the left flank, Nusa did well to beat veteran shot-stopper Karl Darlow with a low drive from the top of the 18-yard box to break the deadlock after the half-time interval. It was Nusa's 10th goal for Norway, and the first for his country since the pair he bagged over the summer across the Atlantic. His pace outwide, competence on the ball, and ability to drive play forward at speed have been at the forefront of Norway's rekindling efforts, and perhaps it's no wonder that Premier League holders and current table-toppers Arsenal have recently been heavily linked with the former Club Brugge standout. Having started alongside the aforementioned Haaland and Ødegaard, as well as Fulham's Oscar Bobb tonight, will Nusa add his name to Norway's Premier League-based ranks come the opening of the January window?

item.title: 'I was envious': R Ashwin makes honest confession about Ravindra Jadeja
item.description: Ravichandran Ashwin has offered an interesting account of what made his bowling partnership with Ravindra Jadeja so successful, revealing how he learned to use the left-arm spinner's strengths and limitations to his advantage. Ashwin described Jadeja as an exceptionally gifted cricketer but suggested that the all-rounder initially lacked the instinct to consistently find ways to dismiss batters. The two formed one of the most successful spin combinations in Test cricket, sharing the field in 58 matches and accounting for 587 wickets. While Ashwin claimed 317 of those dismissals, Jadeja contributed 270. According to the former India off-spinner, their success stemmed from understanding each other's contrasting approaches and making the most of them. Speaking on Aakash Chopra's podcast show, Baith & Bol, Ashwin explained that he understood Jadeja's game well enough to help him operate within his strengths rather than push him towards something that did not come naturally to him. “I know his limitations well," Ashwin said. “Very few can bring him out of those limitations. I was one of them. His biggest strength: naturally gifted. If he has a bad day, you just tell him your effort is fine; tomorrow will be better. His action was simple, release point simple, tappa so good—he doesn’t have to think. He didn’t know how to dismiss batsmen—I’m saying he absolutely didn’t know. But his skill to choke batsmen was intertwined with his skill. You can’t sweep him—trajectory is low. You can’t step out—airspeed is good. You can’t play defense without doubting if the ball would remain the same." One aspect of Jadeja's bowling that often came under scrutiny was his reluctance to vary his pace or give the ball more flight, even when the conditions called for it. Ashwin revealed that he had attempted to persuade his spin partner to experiment more, but those efforts often came at the expense of Jadeja's effectiveness and economy. Eventually, Ashwin recognised that Jadeja's ability to keep things tight from one end gave him the freedom to attack from the other. While Jadeja restricted the opposition's scoring opportunities, Ashwin could experiment with different deliveries and concentrate on taking wickets. That combination also made Jadeja more difficult to deal with. Ashwin said developing this understanding gave him even greater appreciation for what Jadeja brought to the team, particularly his remarkable consistency and control. “When I understood that, my respect for Jadeja doubled—what he does is not easy. I have seen many skillful spinners, but the repetitive nature- keeping the ball there at the same speed is very difficult. Spinning the ball at that speed is not easy," he said. item.title: 'We've waited 73 years to be here' - Wales fans ecstatic after win over New Zealand
item.description: Saturday marked the first time Wales had beaten New Zealand in 73 years [Getty Images] Welsh rugby fans were "fizzing off their heads" on Saturday night after ending 73 years of hurt against New Zealand in an epic Nations Championship encounter. The match at the Principality Stadium ended 35-28 to the hosts as the All Blacks' run of 34 successive victories against Wales - dating back to 1953 - came to a juddering halt in Cardiff. Wales fans were left stunned by a result that came just a week on from having to grind out a win against Japan. Celebrities were also quick to congratulate the team with Gavin & Stacey star Ruth Jones sharing her disbelief in an Instagram post. Three times Wales led by 14 points, and for the first time in history they scored five tries against New Zealand, but ultimately it was heroic defensive work that denied the visitors. All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie made eight changes from the side that swept past Scotland in their previous Nations Championship game. But the approach backfired spectacularly after a brilliant performance sparked astonishing scenes in Cardiff. Darren Williams went to Caernarfon Rugby Club to watch the match [BBC] Darren Williams lives abroad but comes home once a year to visit his family in Wales. He came to Caernarfon Rugby Club to watch the match and said the result was "excellent". "I hope they can continue like this and keep moving forward," he said. "The atmosphere was excellent and very enthusiastic." Daron Owens said she was "really glad" to be at the rugby club to witness such a brilliant performance. "It was great to see everyone so proud. Everyone was cheering so loudly, it was a really positive place to be." One fan pitch side at Principality Stadium said they had waited "73 years to be at this game", adding that they were in "total shock but absolutely delighted". Daron Owens said everyone at the rugby club was "ecstatic" after the game [BBC] Celebrities and politicians were also quick to pay tribute to the team for their heroics on the field. Gavin and Stacey star Jones shared her sheer delight in an Instagram video, with the actor looked visibly stunned following the incredible win over New Zealand. Welsh politicians have also come forward to congratulate the team, including First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth. "This has been decades in the making. Huge congratulations to you all," he wrote on Facebook. "You should all be proud." Secretary of State for Wales Stephen Kinnock said he managed to watch the final part of the game after speaking at the Welsh Labour conference in Llandudno. "After 73 years we've finally beaten the All Blacks! Can barely believe what I've just witnessed," he said. item.title: All Blacks ran into a Welsh brick wall - Barrett
item.description: Beauden Barrett won his 149th New Zealand cap against Wales [Press Association] Beauden Barrett said it felt like New Zealand were running into a red brick wall after they became the first All Blacks side to lose to Wales since 1953. Steve Tandy's men created history with a 35-28 victory at Principality Stadium thanks to a stirring defensive effort. Wales scored five tries - a national record against New Zealand - but it was their effort without the ball that ended a 34-game losing streak against the All Blacks. The home side made 346 tackles, with lock Dafydd Jenkins topping the chart with 38, and held the New Zealanders up over the line three times in the second half to protect their seven-point lead. "It felt like a brick wall at times, so you have to give them credit," said full-back Barrett, who captained New Zealand in a Test for the first time. "You give opportunities for the crowd to come into the game, and we are well aware of that when we come here. "That's why it's one of the best places to play rugby - it feels like you are playing 16 or 17." Magnificent Wales end 73-year New Zealand hoodoo Wales believed they could create history - Lake As it happened: Wales claim first win over New Zealand since 1953 Dave Rennie claimed an unwanted piece of history as the first All Blacks coach to lose to Wales in 73 years. The former Glasgow boss admitted New Zealand "certainly got out-passioned" but had no regrets about his selection. The All Blacks made eight changes to their starting line-up between their win against Scotland and their trip to England in the final Nations Championship group game. "We had a good enough side on the field to win, and if you look at the stats, we had plenty of opportunities and the guys created a lot of chances," said Rennie. "We just weren't clinical enough, and they were very good defensively. "I have no regret around the side that we picked, as I've talked about previously, there is really good competition for places. "There's not a lot between certain positions." Beaten All Blacks climb above Springboks Eddie James started alongside Max Llewellyn for the second time for Wales [Press Association] New Zealand still inched above South Africa, who lost a thriller in France on Friday, into top spot in the southern hemisphere table. If the All Blacks win with a bonus point at Twickenham on Saturday (14:10 GMT), they will secure top spot before the Springboks' game in Ireland (20:10 GMT). "It hurts, but you've got to take it on the chin," said Rennie, who took over from Scott Robertson at the start of the year. "We weren't good enough; Wales were passionate and every time they kept us out, they grew and became harder to break down. "We've got to be better, we expect a lot more of ourselves, and I need to see a response at Twickenham."

item.title: Bears Paid High Price For Simmons, But He Is The Real Prize
item.description: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears did not wait until the final hours of the trade deadline to make their move. They secured the best defensive player in the NFL two weeks before the deadline arrived. To acquire All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, General Manager Ryan Poles traded two first-round picks to the Tennessee Titans, according to Bleacher Nation . The Simmons trade stands apart from every other transaction that happened this week. While other teams swapped veterans for late picks, Chicago bought a cornerstone for the next four years. The Cost of a Game-Wrecker The price tag drew immediate criticism from some analysts. The Bears received a C grade from ESPN, which contended that the team exceeded the point where the compensation remained sensible. That cost comprised the 2027 and 2028 first-round picks alongside a 2027 fourth-rounder. The team did get a 2028 fifth-round pick back. But the value lies in who Simmons is, not just the draft capital spent. He is 29 years old and a four-time Pro Bowler. After logging a career-high 11 sacks last season, he secured his first first-team All-Pro nod. Prior to the trade, ESPN listed him as the interior lineman with the highest pass rush win rate. Seth Walder and Ben Solak at ESPN called him the best defensive tackle in the league, period. That assessment carries weight when looking at the rest of the board. Simmons Versus The Rest Other teams made moves for players who are past their prime. Kirk Cousins is now a Viking. Keenan Allen is a 49er. Josh Downs is in Kansas City. Marvin Harrison Jr. is in Houston. Jessie Bates is in Jacksonville. The best counterargument points to DeForest Buckner, who the 49ers landed for a 2027 fourth-round pick. Buckner is 32 and currently in the final year of his contract. This season, his pass rush win rate has fallen to the 45th percentile. That is down from the 90th percentile a year ago. He is a nice rental for a contender. Simmons is a player you build around for years. The 49ers paid for a few months of a good player. The Bears paid for years of a great one. The contract situation adds another layer to the deal. The Titans had recently extended Simmons and had already paid the bonus. Consequently, Chicago owes him $7.94 million for the remainder of this season plus $26.95 million in future guarantees. Chicago now possesses a player who has accumulated 10 tackles, including three tackles for loss, in only two games. He has also recorded two sacks, two QB hits, and two pass breakups. His presence has demanded double teams, which opens the door for teammates like Montez Sweat and Austin Booker to feast. The Bears are 7-2 and sit atop the NFC North. If they keep winning, those two first-round picks will land somewhere in the high 20s.

item.title: Avalanche Lose MacKinnon for Extended Time, Makar for Two Weeks
item.description: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect The Colorado Avalanche will be without superstars Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar for an extended period. Avalanche head coach Jared Bednar told reporters in Montreal on Saturday morning that MacKinnon is out for at least a month, while Makar is expected to miss two weeks. Both players suffered lower-body injuries in Ottawa, with the incidents occurring around a minute apart in the second period. To replace MacKinnon in the lineup , Colorado recalled forward Gavin Brindley from the American Hockey League on Saturday. The Denver Post’s Corey Masisak confirmed that Brock Nelson will move up to the top line in MacKinnon’s absence, while Nic Roy will center a line with Gabe Landeskog . Nazem Kadri will center another line. On defense, rookie Alex Gagne will make his NHL debut alongside Brent Burns, who is set to appear in his 1,600th career regular-season game. That likely means Noah Juulsen moves up to play with Brett Kulak, leaving Devon Toews and Sam Malinski together as the top pair. The top power play will also have Toews and Artturi Lehkonen on it. They’ll join Martin Necas, T.J. Hughes, and Kadri, as they did after Thursday’s injuries . MacKinnon is Colorado’s top point producer, recording 10 goals, 20 assists, and 30 points in 20 games this season. Makar, who previously missed a game for the birth of his twin children, has five goals and 23 points in 19 games. This is a rare situation for Colorado. Saturday’s matchup against the Canadiens will mark just the seventh time that both superstars have been unavailable for the same game since Makar made his NHL debut. It’s also the first time since March 2021 that both players will miss the same game outside of occasional late-season rest ahead of the playoffs. Bednar said Makar’s injury is soft tissue-related and that there is no concern it will linger beyond the current recovery timeline. The timing offers the Avalanche at least a little relief. item.title: Benatia: ‘Ronaldo asked me to speak to Allegri at Juventus about skipping pre-match retreats’
item.description: Benatia: ‘Ronaldo asked me to speak to Allegri at Juventus about skipping pre-match retreats’ Medhi Benatia has revealed how Cristiano Ronaldo’s dislike of pre-match retreats led to a conversation with Massimiliano Allegri during their time together at Juventus. With quotes via Calciomercato.com , the former Morocco defender told the story to Canal+. Italian clubs traditionally keep their squads together in a hotel or at the training ground the night before matches, known as the ritiro, and Ronaldo found it hard to adjust when he arrived from Real Madrid in 2018. “In 2018 Cristiano Ronaldo arrived, and he didn’t really like the ritiro because he wasn’t used to it,” Benatia said. “He said to me: ‘Isn’t there a way to talk to the Italians a bit, to the coach?’ I replied: ‘Yes, of course, we’ll try.’ “So I went to Chiellini and said: ‘Gio, there’s this teammate who doesn’t really appreciate the ritiro and everything that comes with it.’ He asked: ‘Why? Did he tell you that?’ I said: ‘Yes, he came to me.’ “So we went to speak to the coach, Allegri at the time, together with Chiellini: ‘Mister, there are three or four players, especially the big players, who would prefer not to do the ritiro, if possible.’ The coach replied: ‘Whoever wants to go on the ritiro goes, whoever doesn’t want to doesn’t go.’” TURIN, ITALY – AUGUST 14: Cristiano Ronaldo of Juventus looks on during the pre-season friendly match between Juventus and Atalanta BC at Allianz Stadium on August 14, 2021 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Emilio Andreoli/Getty Images) Benatia on Ronaldo and his Juventus move Benatia spent two and a half years with the Bianconeri, from 2016 to January 2019, winning two Scudetti, two Coppa Italia titles and a Supercoppa Italiana. He joined from Bayern Munich, where he never settled. “I wanted to leave after the first year, so I asked to go. I wanted to come back to Italy. Juve, Inter and other clubs were interested,” he explained. “After two months in Germany, I said to my wife: ‘Listen, I don’t know if I made the right choice here. I don’t feel comfortable. Italy is my second home.’ Medhi Benatia (@m.benatia5 via Instagram) “So I came back and joined Juve. That’s when you see how important work culture and discipline are.”

item.title: NFL Rumors: Green Bay Packers Pursued Trade for Starting RB, Balked at Club’s High Asking Price
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Green Bay Packers have the worst rushing offense in the NFL this season, ranking last in rushing yards per game (68.2) with the second-lowest yards per carry average (3.0). Hoping to improve things with Josh Jacobs out multiple weeks, general manager Brian Gutekunst reportedly pursued a deal for a new starting running back. According to ESPN ‘s Adam Schefter, Green Bay and the Denver Broncos both inquired with the Tennessee Titans regarding the availability of running back Tony Pollard. Tennessee was open to dealing the 29-year-old running back, who is in a contract year, but the asking price reportedly pushed Green Bay and Denver away. Tony Pollard stats (2026): 595 rushing yards, 6 rushing touchdowns, 4.5 yards per carry The Titans front office made it clear that Pollard wouldn’t be moved for anything less than a third-round pick. From Tennessee’s perspective, Pollard’s recent stretch of success (322 rushing yards and 5.0 yards per carry in last three games) was instrumental in the improved play as of late from quarterback Cam Ward. Unless Green Bay or Denver was willing to overpay for a half season of Pollard, a deal wouldn’t be made. It’s the second running back Green Bay has been connected to in NFL trade rumors. Even before Jacobs’ injury, the Packers reportedly inquired with the Indianapolis Colts regarding All-Pro running back Jonathan Taylor. While he was technically available, Indianapolis wanted a first-round pick for him or multiple Day 2 picks in the 2027 NFL Draft and future draft capital. The Micah Parsons trade leaves Green Bay without a first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Gutekunst’s draft capital took another blow this week when the Miami Dolphins placed quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve. Because he’s now expected to miss at least four games, the projected third-round compensatory pick Green Bay anticipated receiving for Miami signing him will likely now be a fourth-round selection in 2027. Ultimately, Gutekunst just couldn’t justify sacrificing all of his Day 2 picks and additional assets for Taylor nor was he willing to give up a third-round pick for half a season of Pollard. Given that Green Bay’s offensive line has been one of the biggest reasons for the run game’s struggles, that could prove to be the right decision.
